messages:
From: Sarah Liu <security@greenriver.health>
To: Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwood.ai>
Cc: GreenRiver Compliance Team <compliance@greenriver.health>
Date: Wed, 18 Jun 2025 08:10:00 -0700
Subject: Request: admin activity evidence for SOC 2 / SIG review

Hi Rishi —

We're preparing for a SIG questionnaire and our external auditors are asking for admin-activity evidence for the period Jan 1, 2025 — Jun 1, 2025. Specifically they want:
- a CSV manifest of admin actions (create/delete/role-change/login-as) with event_id, actor_id, target_id, action_type, timestamp (ISO8601), region, and workflow_id
- confirmation of retention policies and whether events older than 90 days are archived or truncated
- recommended redaction approach for user-facing PII (email/email hashes vs full email) and guidance on timestamp fidelity (original vs normalized)

Can you confirm:
1) what export formats you can provide (CSV/NDJSON/parquet)
2) whether you can produce a point-in-time snapshot and a differential stream (e.g., incremental since a snapshot)
3) options for partial deliveries with redaction and HMAC manifests for integrity verification

We'd like an example manifest and a short playbook describing the delivery options we can present to auditors by EOD Monday.

Thanks,
Sarah
Security & Compliance
GreenRiver Health

Sarah — thanks for the clear list. Looping in Vanessa (privacy/compliance) and Kim (platform ops) to confirm formats and delivery windows. Quick responses inline: 

1) Formats: we can produce CSV and NDJSON natively; parquet is available as an export conversion (adds ~2-4% processing time).

2) Snapshot vs differential: we can deliver a full point-in-time snapshot (gzipped tarball) and follow with an incremental delta stream (NDJSON) covering the subsequent window. Snapshots preserve event sequence numbers for replay.

3) Redaction/HMAC: two common patterns — (A) Full export to a secure S3 bucket with an attached HMAC manifest and signed delivery; (B) Filtered export with PII redaction (hashes for emails, truncated IPs) plus a redaction matrix that documents transformation.

I'm attaching a short note with the delivery options and an example manifest header to get auditors started. Vanessa/Kim — can you confirm the default retention policy for admin events and any caveats re: ephemeral operator traces?

Next steps: Vanessa to confirm retention and legal constraints; Kim to propose a timeline and include sample manifest. If GreenRiver prefers, we can schedule a 30-minute handoff to walk through the manifest.

Best,
Rishi
Director, Customer Security (on behalf of Redwood Inference)

Hi Sarah / team —

Thanks for the request. A few clarifications and commitments from the compliance side: 

- Retention: admin activity (operator/admin actions) is retained at full fidelity for 180 days by default. After 180 days events are compressed into archived snapshots that preserve event_id, action_type, timestamp (UTC), and a compressed payload. We can extend retention under a contract addendum (committed retention cohorts).

- Ephemeral traces: certain ephemeral debug artifacts (e.g., ephemeral KV-cache traces used for debugging model runs) are excluded from the standard admin activity export by default; we can include them on request but they require an ops-level sign-off.

- Redaction policy: for customer-facing exports we recommend hashing email addresses with an HMAC (per-customer key) and removing session tokens; maintain original timestamps in UTC but include a normalized_time column (ISO8601) for auditor workflows. The redaction_matrix.xlsx I'm attaching maps columns -> recommended transformation.

Delivery options we can support:
A) Full snapshot to an S3 bucket (encrypted) + signed HMAC manifest + SHA256 checksums for each file.
B) Filtered snapshot with PII redacted + redaction matrix + HMAC manifest.
C) Sample + schema + sample manifest (for quick SIG review) — we can stage a 48-hour sample export within 24 hours.

I'll prepare the redaction matrix and confirm legal approvals for the full snapshot option. Rishi / Kim: please propose the on-call window for transfer and an estimate for creating a sample snapshot.

Regards,
Vanessa Ortiz
Senior Legal Operations
Redwood Inference

Sarah — technical follow-up with concrete options and sample manifest header. Apologies for the long note; calling out options so auditors can pick what they need.

Export formats we will include: CSV (UTF-8, newline LF), NDJSON (one event per line), and compressed parquet on request. Each export is accompanied by an index manifest with the following header columns: file_name, sha256_checksum, event_count, sequence_start, sequence_end, earliest_timestamp_utc, latest_timestamp_utc.

Sample manifest row (CSV header):
file_name,sha256_checksum,event_count,sequence_start,sequence_end,earliest_timestamp_utc,latest_timestamp_utc
admin_activity_20250101_20250601.part-0001.ndjson,3b9c...,124597,100001,224598,2025-01-01T00:00:12Z,2025-06-01T23:59:58Z

Event schema (common fields):
- event_id (uuid)
- sequence (monotonic integer)
- actor_id (redwood_user_id)
- actor_role (admin/operator/service)
- action_type (CREATE, DELETE, ROLE_CHANGE, ELEVATE, DELEGATE, LOGIN_AS, TOKEN_ISSUE)
- target_id (resource id)
- payload (JSON blob)
- timestamp_utc (ISO8601)
- normalized_time (ISO8601)
- region (string)

Preserving sequence: snapshots include sequence numbers to enable deterministic replay. For large exports we chunk by time window (default 7-day chunks) and by file size (~1GB compressed). We can change chunking on request.

Sampling: for SIG-level review we usually provide a 1% stratified sample plus full manifest; if auditors request, we can instead provide a 100% sample for a targeted 30-day window. Sampling scripts and seed are included so auditors can reproduce the exact sample.

Transfer: options are S3 presigned URLs (preferred), SFTP with client cert, or a signed AWS Snowball (for extremely large datasets). We'll provide HMAC manifests and per-file SHA256 checksums for integrity.

Estimate: sample snapshot (48-hour sample) — ~6 business hours to stage and validate. Full snapshot for the six-month window — 2 business days (subject to queue).

Kim
Platform Ops Lead
Redwood Inference
